                ;**********************************************************************
                ; Purpose: external phase-transition target. JMP $4000 at $02FA leaves the EA autostart and enters the TITLE image, whose own entry veneer at $4000 jumps to title_phase_main at $4003; TITLE is modelled in program 10_TITLE_protection_transition_raw.bin, so this program shows $4000 as uninitialized. Inputs: TITLE already loaded at $4000-$509F by the KERNAL LOAD at $02F4 and all KERNAL channels closed by CLALL at $02F7. Outputs: control never returns to the autostart; the autostart's 56 bytes at $02CC-$0303 are dead from this point. Assumptions: the load succeeded and KERNAL ROM plus I/O are still visible, which the autostart never changes. Clobbers: everything TITLE clobbers; the autostart keeps nothing live across the transfer. Hardware changes: none by the jump itself; the autostart leaves $D021=$01, $D020=$01, the screen cleared by CHROUT $93 and KERNAL messages suppressed by SETMSG.

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; Purpose: put the VIC-II into ordinary hires text mode in VIC bank 2 and tell the KERNAL where the matrix is. Called from title_phase_main $4015 and from restore_text_screen $4061. Inputs: none; all values are immediate. Outputs: text display selected, sprites off, and $0288=$8C so KERNAL screen output writes to $8C00. Assumptions: I/O is visible so $D0xx and $DDxx name registers rather than RAM, and CIA2 port A may be reprogrammed because no serial transfer is in progress. Clobbers: A and flags. Hardware changes: $D015=$00 disables all sprites; $D011=$1B selects text mode with the display enabled, RSEL set and YSCROLL 3; $D018=$34 selects matrix offset $0C00 and character generator offset $1000; $D016=$C8 selects hires 40-column with XSCROLL 0; $DD02 |= $03 makes CIA2 PA0/PA1 outputs; $DD00 = (old & $FC) | $01 selects VIC bank 2, $8000-$BFFF, because the bank bits are inverted, placing the matrix at $8C00 and the character generator at $9000; $0288 = $8C.
                ;**********************************************************************

                ; XREF[2]: 4015(c), 4061(c)

It derives bytes $4C,$8A,$FF from loaded stack data, writes JMP $FF8A at $033C-$033E, invokes KERNAL RESTOR, clears the display through internal CHROUT, stores protection breadcrumbs, and jumps to $0125. Inputs: entry $0203; exact loaded bytes in $013C-$023B. Outputs: default KERNAL vectors restored before LOADER overwrites them; $0286=$01 and $009D=$01. Assumptions: NMOS 6510 semantics for LAX, SAX and undocumented NOPs. Clobbers: A,X,Y and $033C-$033E. Hardware/state: border/background become white; screen is cleared.

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; Purpose: three bytes assembled at run time in the cassette buffer and immediately called, so that the KERNAL RESTOR call never appears as a literal JSR in the file. Built and entered by construct_restor_trampoline_fragment: $020A stores the byte at $033D, $0214 stores the byte at $033E, $021A stores the byte at $033C, and $021D calls $033C. Inputs: the three bytes are fetched by table-indexed reads whose indices chain through the file's own bytes: X starts as the value at $015A, which is $4C; $0206 reads $01C5+X giving $8A; $020D reads $019C+$8A giving $FF; $0217 reads $013C+$FF giving $4C. Outputs: $033C-$033E holds exactly 4C 8A FF, that is JMP $FF8A, so the JSR at $021D reaches KERNAL RESTOR, which reinstalls the default I/O vectors at $0314-$0333, and RESTOR's own RTS returns to $0220. Assumptions: KERNAL ROM is visible at the moment of the call; the listing shows $033C-$033E as uninitialized because the bytes exist only at run time, not in the file. Clobbers: A, X, flags, the three bytes at $033C-$033E, and the whole KERNAL RAM vector table rewritten by RESTOR. Hardware changes: none directly; RESTOR rewrites RAM vectors only. Verified by exact-byte derivation from the retained $00F7-$0245 image.
                ;**********************************************************************

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; Purpose: KERNAL CHROUT, output the byte in A to the current output device. This is the ROM entry the IBSOUT vector at $0326 points to; mapping_the_commodore_64_and_c64c/07-kernal-rom.md:578 records '61898 ($F1CA) CHROUT - Output a Byte', and :948 records $FFD2 vectoring through $0326 to $F1CA. Inputs: A holds the character or control code; the current output channel is whatever CHKOUT last selected, here the default screen. Outputs: the character is emitted; A is preserved by KERNAL CHROUT. Assumptions: KERNAL ROM is banked in at the moment of the call, which the $01 value in force during the stack-loader phase satisfies. This is NOT a clear-screen routine: the single call at $0231 clears the screen only because the preceding undocumented LAX $0200 at $022E loads A=X from $0200, whose value in the retained $00F7-$0245 image is $93, the PETSCII clear-screen code. With any other A it outputs that character instead. Clobbers: as documented for KERNAL CHROUT; X and Y are preserved, processor flags and KERNAL screen-editor workspace are not. Hardware changes: whatever the selected output device performs; for the screen editor, writes to the video matrix and colour RAM and updates the KERNAL cursor variables.
                ;**********************************************************************

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; Purpose: fixed transfer target of JMP $8009 at final_decrypted_protection_payload::$FCFE, taken when the second byte of a received destination pair is $00. Unlike the ordinary exit, this path does not restore $01=$37 and does not use the patched zero-page exit stub, so the destination is entered with the protection's own banking still selected. Inputs: none beyond the received command. Outputs: control leaves the serial engine permanently. Assumptions, inferred and not verified: $8009 is the byte after a cartridge-style CBM80 header at $8000, the same cold-start entry the dormant C128 bootstrap in RESERVED BY EA installs when it copies 256 bytes to $8000; the game image is therefore expected to be resident there. Clobbers: determined by the destination. Hardware changes: none by the jump itself. TODO - no capture in this project shows $8000-$800F populated, and the observed success route did not take this branch. Resolving experiment: break at $FCFE on the reproducible route with $01=$15 and dump $8000-$8020, or force the branch by supplying a $00 high byte and record where execution lands.

                ; Purpose: fifth interior onion transform loop; XOR one byte of the remaining tail with two live CIA2 Timer A samples and a stage constant, store it back, and repeat until Y wraps. Outputs: $F408-$FEFF advanced by one XOR layer, one page per outer iteration. Assumptions: exact NMOS timing, because the two EOR operands are read from a free-running timer; and the pass never rewrites $F400-$F407, which is why those eight bytes stay at the previous layer. Clobbers: A, Y, flags and the transformed bytes. Hardware changes: reads CIA2 Timer A low $DD04 and high $DD05 once per byte; writes nothing outside RAM. TODO - the two bytes at $F401-$F402 in the retained capture are stale ciphertext. Every other interior stage places a two-byte third-key EOR here (EOR #$45, #$4F, #$21, #$2E, #$4B, #$48, or EOR $32 / EOR $33), and the surrounding template forces EOR $DD05 at $F3FE-$F400, STA ($2B),Y at $F403, INY at $F405 and BNE $F3F9 at $F406-$F407. Resolving experiment: on the reproducible route, break at $F408 or $F40F with $01=$15 and read $F400-$F407; the $F3DD pass has completed by then and the erase loop at $F40F has not yet overwritten $F3E4-$F40E.                 ; Second stale sub-page window, independent confirmation of the same mechanism. The retained composite capture holds 03 61 DF 51 73 5C C0 49 4F 44 at $F500-$F509.
